ordering_diagnostic.what: rank of native Stockfish's deep best move inside our 40k-node root ordering
ordering_diagnostic.self_reference: our own 1.5M-node best move is rank 1 in 13/24 positions, rank >10 in 4/24
ordering_diagnostic.reading: any movecount/SEE pruning at depth cuts the engine's own eventual best move about a third of the time

conclusion: Selectivity buys +3 nominal plies at 40k nodes and is strength-neutral PER NODE at 40k, but strength-NEGATIVE at the budgets the engine plays at (12k nodes: -51 Elo, LLR -2.945; equal time 3+0.03: -95 Elo, LLR -2.958) -- the smaller the node budget the worse it gets. Root cause measured: move ordering (SF's deep best move sits past rank 10 in ~1/3 of positions; first-move cutoff 45% vs SF ~90%) and eval accuracy (~172cp static MAE vs SF), so every movecount/SEE/eval cut discards the engine's own best move. Depth-per-node is not a strength currency for this engine: the lever is eval + ordering, not selectivity.
